subject: FW: Request for downtime validation and proposed prorated credit schedule
messages:
From: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@rapidretail.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@rapidretail.com
Date: Tue, 27 Oct 2026 23:46:12 -0700
Subject: Site-wide 500s during peak — potential SLA claim

Evelyn,

We saw a sharp spike in 500s across checkout and product-search between 2026-10-27T20:12:00Z and 2026-10-27T20:34:00Z (our metrics are UTC). That window caused roughly 12% of checkout requests to fail and impacted peak revenue. I attached a screenshot from our monitoring and a short error sample.

Can you please:
- Confirm whether Redwood observed a regional service disruption in us-west-2 during that UTC window
- Tell us whether this qualifies under the SLA for a remedy and what the next steps are to get a credit
- Provide a timeline for postmortem and any interim mitigations we should take

We rely on the 99.95% availability in our contract and this materially affected orders.

Thanks,
Marta Ruiz
Head of Platform — Rapid Retail

Attachments:
- rri_500s_screenshot_10-27.png (image)
- sample-errors.txt (text)

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>

Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 27 Oct 2026 23:58:40 -0700
Subject: Re: Site-wide 500s during peak — potential SLA claim

Hi Marta — thanks for the report and the timing. We're looking into this now.

Quick notes / next steps:
- I've looped in David (runtime) and Laura (SRE) to validate telemetry and pull the raw traces/log bundle.
- Can you grant permission to share a sanitized log bundle back to your team and to publish a non-sensitive postmortem once complete? We will redact any tenant-identifying fields.
- We expect an initial confirmation on eligibility and a proposed remedy (if any) within 12 business hours. If it looks like an SLA-eligible availability window, we'll propose a prorated credit and schedule a postmortem invite.

Laura/David — please prioritize a verification of the 20:12–20:34 UTC window; if you need specific correlation ids from Rapid Retail, Marta, the sample-errors.txt has two.

I'll follow up shortly with a timeline.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Head of Customer Success
Redwood Inference

Attachment referenced: None (we will attach log bundle after validation)

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 08:07:05 -0700
Subject: Internal: Rapid Retail — validate 500-window and classify for SLA remedy

David/Laura,

Forwarding Rapid Retail's report (below). Key asks:
1) Confirm whether we observed a service availability regression affecting tenant routing in us-west-2 between 2026-10-27T20:12:00Z and 2026-10-27T20:34:00Z.
2) If yes, provide a short description of the root cause or contributing factor (e.g., autoscaler thrash, preemption, control-plane evict) and whether the failure mode maps to an SLA uptime breach.
3) Produce a sanitized log bundle (rri_request_logs_20261027.zip) that we can send back to Marta. Keep PII/tenant ids redacted per standard process.
4) Estimate the prorated credit calculation (percent availability delta over billing period) so I can propose an initial remedy to the customer.

Rapid Retail impact appears significant for peak checkout traffic — please mark this as P1. I'll be on call for coordination.

Thanks,
Evelyn

--- Original Message ---
(see message from Marta Ruiz sent 2026-10-27 23:46)

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@rapidretail.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Site-wide 500s during peak — potential SLA claim (confirmation & remedy)

Marta — thank you for the patience. Summary of what we've validated and proposed next steps: 

1) Confirmed downtime window (UTC): 2026-10-27T20:11:55Z – 2026-10-27T20:34:12Z. Our telemetry (us-west-2 ingress + request-trace sampling) shows elevated 5xx rates and increased request timeouts correlated with a transient autoscaler instability on a subset of GPU-backed pools.

2) Classification against the contract: The incident caused a regional availability delta that meets the SLA definition of a service interruption for the affected tenants. We've marked this as eligible for remedy under the 99.95% availability commitment.

3) Proposed remedy: Initial prorated credit equivalent to 8.5% of the monthly bill for the affected month (calculation attached). This is our provisional offer pending final audit of the billing window. If you prefer, we can roll this into an account credit or apply as a one-time invoice adjustment; let me know which you prefer.

4) Postmortem & timing: Engineering (David/Laura) will prepare a redacted log bundle and a technical RCA within 72 hours. I'm attaching the log bundle (rri_request_logs_20261027.zip) with tenant ids redacted and an invite to a 60-minute postmortem review: postmortem-invite.ics. We'll also produce a public-safe one-page summary after redaction.

5) Next steps for you: Please confirm that Redwood may share the redacted logs back to your ops team and whether you prefer a credit on next invoice or an immediate refund/adjustment. We'll finalize the exact credit after the audit but wanted to get the timeline and proposed amount to you ASAP.

If you want the SRE/eng folks on the call earlier, we can move up the postmortem — otherwise we'll meet at the scheduled slot in the invite.

Apologies again for the disruption. We're treating this with high priority and will follow through on the RCA and remediation steps.

Best regards,
Evelyn Hart
Head of Customer Success
Redwood Inference

Attachments sent: rri_request_logs_20261027.zip (sanitized log bundle), postmortem-invite.ics (calendar invite)
